scope: Independent bounded static audit of Preview crop interaction, source/PDF coordinate conversion, render identity, source mutation and Undo path; read-only review of native harness and its output image/log. No production code edits and no independent claim of executing the parent-owned native test.
verdict: No remaining concrete blocker in the reviewed implementation.

findings_fixed_before_final_review.finding: A drag started in one PDF transform could survive a direct PDFKit scroll or zoom and commit using coordinates from a different transform.
findings_fixed_before_final_review.resolution: PDFView scale/page/visible-page notifications and clip bounds changes now cancel the draft. Root native harness directly changes PDF zoom and scroll origin during a drag and checks that no edit occurs.

findings_fixed_before_final_review.finding: The overlay is a sibling of PDFView; sending scrollWheel to PDFView need not route to its internal NSScrollView.
findings_fixed_before_final_review.resolution: The overlay cancels its draft and forwards scrolling directly to PDFView.documentView.enclosingScrollView. Root harness verifies real clip-origin movement.

reviewed_invariants: The PDFDocument, exact render plan used by the exporter and source snapshot publish together in one PublishedPreview value.
canEdit rejects in-flight and stale snapshots; the crop callback also rechecks both source snapshot and exact original band before mutation.

PDFKit conversions handle PDF bottom-up versus flipped overlay coordinates. CropGeometry maps output delta through actual placement scale and original source-page height, validates matching vertical source geometry, and clamps without moving the opposite edge.

Dragging updates only overlay draft state. One mouse-up callback commits a single ordinary Resize Band source transaction; Esc, layout resize, selection, source replacement and transform changes discard draft state.

Document updateBand preserves absolute source whiteout positions, intersects them with the resized crop and includes that adjustment in the same Undo transaction. Generated rests and nonfinite input cannot be resized.
Non-crop PDF interactions pass through the overlay when no editable strip/handle is hit. The overlay supports scrolling and pinch zoom over its own hit regions.
After PDF reflow the same selected band anchors its prior viewport offset when it remains present; manual zoom is retained.

Selection alone is outside renderer snapshot identity. Per-event dragging does not rebuild a PDF. Overlay rebuild/hit search is linear in selected-part band count; this review did not benchmark very large parts.

validation_evidence.native_ui: Parent-owned offscreen AppKit/PDFKit harness log reports PASS: 34 native Preview interaction checks. Independently read its test code and passing log, including direct transform cancellation, real scroll routing, source-coordinate conversion, one-commit drag, Esc, stale rendering, reflow and manual zoom.
validation_evidence.screenshot: Independently inspected preview-crop-drag.png: selected strip outline and two handles track the visible strip; the removed top portion is dimmed. This deliberately broad test band is a gesture fixture, not a claim of automatic musical extraction quality.
validation_evidence.other_tests_reported_by_parent: Core 110, existing layout 5389 and export 169 checks pass; those runs were not rerun by this reviewer.
validation_evidence.native_log_warning: The native test log contains a PDFKit timed page-drawing warning before the PASS line; the captured overlay image was readable and all 34 assertions passed.

limits: No active user app or document was modified by this review.
The native harness is offscreen and programmatically sends real AppKit mouse events; it is not a human trackpad acceptance session.
No broad extraction algorithm quality verdict follows from crop gesture correctness.
There is no measured large-score latency claim beyond the code-level invariant that dragging performs no PDF export until commit.
